result.summary:
Wrote both vitest files test-specs/REQ-031.md designed (BACKEND-DEV's own Step 2 handoff committed no test file, per the spec's own independence note), implementing every case verbatim: apps/bot/src/scheduler/feedbackJobs.db.test.ts (AC1/AC4/AC7, tg_id 993_000_000+) and apps/bot/src/handlers/feedback.db.test.ts (AC2/AC3/AC5/S3, tg_id 994_000_000+). AC6 run separately as a shell git grep per the spec's own instruction (not a vitest it()).

npm run lint -w apps/bot: pass, zero output. npm run build -w apps/bot (tsc -p tsconfig.json): pass, zero errors.

npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism from the repo root (ISS-0014's mandated invocation): two consecutive clean runs after a fix (below) both produced 33 test files / 316 tests / 0 failures / 0 skipped. This is the fresh repo-root count being reported, not a number carried over from any earlier step's handoff.

Own defect found and fixed (not a spec/implementation issue): the AC2 raw-duplicate-INSERT assertion originally asserted `.rejects.toMatchObject({ code: '23505' })` directly on the thrown error. drizzle-orm's node-postgres driver wraps the raw pg error one level deep as DrizzleQueryError.cause -- the exact shape domain/notification.ts's own pgErrorCode() helper (lines 86-90) explicitly unwraps. Fixed the test's own assertion to `.rejects.toMatchObject({ cause: { code: '23505' } })` before the final passing runs.

Transient failures investigated and NOT attributed to this run (Failure Attribution Is Structural): an earlier run (before the AC2 fix) additionally showed unrelated failures (connection-pool timeouts) in domain/notification.test.ts, domain/registration.db.test.ts, and handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts -- none of these files are in this branch's diff. Ran the causal experiment core-directives.md requires rather than count-matching to a filed issue: (1) same full suite with this run's two new test files EXCLUDED -> 31/31 files clean; (2) same full suite with them RE-INCLUDED, run again -> 33/33 files clean; (3) a third full run -> 33/33 files clean again. The failures did not reproduce deterministically with or without the new files present, which rules out a simple 'my new files exhausted the connection pool' causal story and instead matches the intermittent scratch-Postgres-contention pattern already on record in ISS-0027 (filed this same run by BACKEND-DEV, MINOR, open) -- reported as flaky/environmental with the actual experiment as evidence, not asserted by resemblance to that filed issue alone.

Spec defect flagged, not silently worked around (per this run's own task instruction and REQ-026 AC4/REQ-028 precedent): AC6's static check as literally specified (`git grep -in "talk|speaker|want to speak"` across schema.ts in full, among other files) produces ONE match -- schema.ts:240's PRE-EXISTING comment '// Array of { kind, at, label } objects — non-talk agenda items only', confirmed via git blame/git log -S to be commit 584707f9 (2026-09-06, REQ-011), predating this branch entirely. This is a false-positive substring hit on 'non-talk' containing 'talk', documenting the opposite fact (agenda items explicitly exclude talks). Re-running the identical grep scoped to only the files REQ-031 actually introduced/touched (domain/feedback.ts, handlers/feedback.ts, scheduler/feedbackJobs.ts, i18n/types.ts, i18n/ru.ts, i18n/en.ts) produces zero matches. The substance of AC6 (no talk/speaker feature or entity was added) is genuinely satisfied; the spec's literal grep command is imprecise about schema.ts's scope. Recommend ORCH file this as a MINOR test-spec-precision issue against test-specs/REQ-031.md for TEST-DESIGNER -- not fixed here, per Instruction Precedence's ban on satisfying a gate by editing what it measures.

All 7 acceptance criteria (AC1-AC7), the S3 exploit's three sub-attacks, and the stale-reply field-match case each have their designed verification case passing. Full per-case results in test-reports/report-2026-09-07-WF02-REQ-031-step04.yaml.

issues.title: test-specs/REQ-031.md's AC6 git grep pattern false-positives on a pre-existing, unrelated schema.ts comment
issues.description: AC6's specified command greps apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts in full for 'talk|speaker|want to speak'. schema.ts:240 carries a pre-existing (REQ-011, commit 584707f9, 2026-09-06) comment '// Array of { kind, at, label } objects — non-talk agenda items only', which matches on the substring 'talk' inside 'non-talk'. This is a false positive -- the comment documents that agenda items explicitly exclude talks, not a talk/speaker feature. Scoping the same grep to only REQ-031's own new/touched files (excluding schema.ts's own pre-existing comment) produces zero matches, confirming the acceptance criterion's substance is satisfied. Recommend either scoping AC6's schema.ts check to just the new `feedback` table definition, or refining the pattern to avoid 'non-talk'.
